key: Before a gully-cricket season, the senior
name: ch16_gully_cricket_chalk_rules
alt: In a colony lane, a teenage captain writes the cricket rules on a wall in chalk while the younger boys call out the rules they want.
scene: A wide view of a narrow colony lane in late afternoon, a plastered compound wall running across the back with a balcony above it and a potted tulsi on the ledge. On the LEFT the senior boy, about sixteen, in a teal T-shirt and shorts, stands at the wall holding a stick of white chalk, writing a short list under a heading; the list is drawn as three short white lines with tick marks next to them. Leaning against the wall is a taped tennis-ball bat and a stump made from a stack of bricks. In the CENTRE and RIGHT four younger boys aged ten to thirteen, in coral, amber, plum and white T-shirts, stand in a loose half-circle, one with his hand raised high, another pointing at the wall, a third holding the ball, all eager rather than sulking. Small speech bubbles above two of the boys show simple icons, a bat with a circular arrow (fair turns) and a cracked window with a coin (whoever breaks pays), connecting by dashed arrows to the chalk lines so it is clear the rules came from them. The captain is turned half toward the boys, listening, not lecturing. Warm golden light, a relaxed summer mood. Label: "OUR RULES" written in chalk-style capitals at the top of the list on the wall.

key: A tailor in Chandni Chowk can hold up
name: ch16_tailor_kurta_choices
alt: A tailor shows a customer cloth and option cards for collar, sleeves and pockets, and the customer happily points to his choices.
scene: A split-panel illustration with a thin vertical divider. LEFT panel: inside a small old-city tailoring shop with bolts of cloth stacked on wooden shelves, a middle-aged tailor with spectacles and a measuring tape around his neck holds up a finished pale-blue kurta at arm's length; the customer, a man in his thirties in a white shirt, stands with arms folded and a doubtful frown, and three small red question-mark badges float around the kurta at the collar, sleeve and pocket to show the small things he will find wrong. RIGHT panel: the same tailor at the same counter, a bolt of the same pale-blue cloth unrolled on the table, and three small option cards laid out: a stand-up collar versus a plain collar, a full sleeve versus a three-quarter sleeve, a pocket versus no pocket. The customer leans in, smiling, finger tapping one card; a green tick sits on each chosen card. The tailor holds his scissors ready, clearly still the craftsman doing the skilled work. Behind them a sewing machine on a side table. Soft warm shop light. Labels: "HIS DESIGN" at the top of the left panel, "YOUR CHOICES" at the top of the right panel.

key: In a joint family in Kochi, one cousin
name: ch16_hampi_trip_niece
alt: A young girl shows her school project on old stone ruins to her aunt, who now points happily to a picture of the ruins on the family trip board while a cousin smiles in the background.
scene: A cosy living room of a Kerala joint-family home with a wooden swing seat, a brass lamp and a window showing coconut palms. In the CENTRE a girl of about nine in a yellow frock holds up a school project chart showing a sketch of a stone chariot and temple ruins, eyes bright with excitement. On the RIGHT her aunt, a woman in her fifties in a plum saree with her hair in a bun, bends toward the chart with a delighted face, one hand on the girl's shoulder and the other pointing to a family trip board on the wall. The trip board shows two cards: one with a beach and palm tree, gently crossed out with a soft grey line, and one with the stone ruins, circled in amber. On the LEFT, partly in the background, the cousin, a young man in his twenties in a teal shirt, sits on the swing with a cup of tea and a quiet small smile, not lobbying, just watching. A dashed arrow runs from the girl's chart to the ruins card on the board, showing that the shared reason came from the child, not the cousin. Warm evening light, a happy family mood. Label: "HAMPI" under the ruins card on the board.

name: ch16_doctor_reviews_leaflet
alt: Outside a clinic a queue of sales reps waves brochures, while inside one rep sits back as the doctor marks up a patient leaflet with a pen.
scene: A clinic seen in cross-section. On the LEFT, outside the clinic door in a corridor with a wooden bench, a queue of four sales representatives in formal shirts and ties stands in a line, each holding up a glossy brochure with a big star on it, and a fifth figure is implied by a shadow at the edge; they look bored and impatient. A small sign on the door reads "OPD". On the RIGHT, inside the consulting room with a steel desk, a stethoscope, a blood-pressure machine and a calendar, an older doctor in his fifties with grey hair, spectacles and a white coat leans over a single folded paper leaflet, pen in hand, making notes and circling words, clearly absorbed and pleased. Across the desk one young rep in a light shirt without a brochure sits back with an open notebook, listening, palms open. A speech bubble from the rep shows an icon of an elderly person with a question mark, and a thought bubble from the doctor shows the leaflet with green ticks. On the doctor's desk the stack of glossy brochures from other reps lies untouched. Calm daytime light. Label: "YOUR ADVICE?" in the rep's speech bubble area at top right.

key: A senior teacher in a Chennai school
name: ch16_principal_takes_idea
alt: In two moments, a senior teacher suggests an idea to a frowning principal over tea, and a week later the principal proudly presents the same idea while the teacher smiles and applauds.
scene: A split-panel illustration with a thin vertical divider. LEFT panel, a quiet staff room with a steel tea tumbler on a table: a senior woman teacher in her fifties in a teal cotton saree with spectacles leans forward, her speech bubble showing four small coloured flags (red, blue, green, yellow) for the school houses; across from her a younger principal, a man in his forties in a white shirt and dark trousers, sits with arms crossed and a frown, and a small grey cloud with a squiggle floats above his head. RIGHT panel, one week later, a staff meeting with a whiteboard: the principal stands proudly at the whiteboard, chest out, pointing to the same four coloured flags drawn on it, with a small light bulb above his head. Seated in the front row, the same senior teacher claps with a warm, genuine smile, one hand half raised to volunteer, while two other teachers nod. A thin dashed amber arrow curves from the flags in her bubble in the left panel to the flags on the whiteboard in the right panel, showing where the idea really came from. Warm school-day light. Labels: "OVER TEA" at the top of the left panel, "A NEW IDEA" at the top of the right panel.

key: Ten PG and hostel owners near a Pune
name: ch16_pg_owner_references
alt: Several hostel owners push flyers at worried parents, while one owner simply hands them a slip with three phone numbers and the father calls one of them.
scene: A street outside a college gate with a row of small hostel buildings in the background. On the LEFT three hostel owners, men in their forties and fifties in shirts and one in a kurta, crowd forward holding out glossy flyers with stars and big smiling icons, their mouths open in sales talk; more flyers lie scattered on the ground to suggest there are ten of them. In the CENTRE a pair of parents from a small town, a father in a checked shirt and a mother in a coral saree with a handbag, stand beside their teenage son carrying a rolling suitcase; the mother looks overwhelmed by the flyers. On the RIGHT a calm owner, a woman in her fifties in a plum salwar suit, stands apart and hands the father a small plain slip of paper with three short lines on it, like phone numbers. The father already has his phone to his ear, and a phone call bubble shows a young student's smiling face with a thumbs up and a small plate of food icon. A dashed line leads from the call bubble to a green tick and a small cash envelope labelled with a key icon, showing the deposit is paid. Evening light. Label: "CALL THEM" above the slip of paper.

key: A good cricket captain at the toss
name: ch16_captain_asks_bowler
alt: On a cricket ground, the captain asks the fast bowler about his plan and then moves fielders to match the plan the bowler draws on a small field card.
scene: A cricket ground in the morning seen from the side, with the pitch strip in the middle and a pavilion with a small roof on the far left in the background. In the FOREGROUND LEFT the captain, a man in his late twenties in a white cricket shirt with a teal cap, stands beside his fast bowler, a taller young man in white with a sweatband, holding the red ball. The captain holds up a small card that shows an oval field diagram; the bowler is pointing at it with one finger, explaining, and the captain is listening and nodding. A speech bubble from the captain shows a simple icon of the two ends of the pitch with a question mark between them. On the RIGHT, in the background, three fielders in white jog to new positions following dashed amber arrows, matching small dots on the card, so it is visible that the field is being set to the bowler's plan. At the far right, near the stumps, the batsman waits with his bat grounded. Bright clear sunlight, a focused and confident mood. Label: "YOUR PLAN?" written near the captain's speech bubble at top.
